requiredFlows.description: The MCP server exposes discoverable tool contracts, workflow guidance, catalogs, and structured result paths before a caller commits to a character or battle workflow.
The MCP surface admits an SRD character creation workflow through create, discover, fill, and finalize tools without relying on support-profile status as scenario evidence.
The MCP surface exposes durable character sheet state and battle handoff results through list and session snapshot tools.
The MCP surface admits an SRD battle flow through start, read, discover acts, fill battle holes, resolve acts, end turns, and end battle tools.

evidence.summary: The protocol acceptance scenario verifies the tool list, schema exposure, workflow guide result paths, catalog discovery, and stat block discovery that let a caller orient before entering a specific workflow.
The protocol acceptance scenario reads the MCP workflow guide and catalog units before selecting the returned level-4 Wizard progression, class feature, hole ids, option ids, and draft revisions.

The protocol acceptance scenario reads the MCP workflow guide and catalog units before selecting the returned level-5 Wizard progression, spellbook, prepared-spell, equipment, loadout, and battle result paths.

The protocol acceptance scenario creates and finalizes a supported level-3 Elf Soldier Wizard through create, discover, fill, and finalize tools while selecting the SRD Evoker subclass plus returned Wizard spellbook, Evocation Savant spellbook, and prepared-spell holes.

The protocol acceptance scenario creates and finalizes a supported level-4 Elf Soldier Wizard while selecting the SRD Evoker subclass, the returned Ability Score Improvement feat choice, the returned Intelligence +2 ASI option, Wizard spell choices, equipment, and loadout holes.

The protocol acceptance scenario creates and finalizes a supported level-5 Elf Soldier Wizard while selecting Fireball only through returned spellbook and prepared-spell option ids plus returned Wizard creation holes.

The protocol acceptance scenario creates and finalizes the supported level-1 Orc Soldier Fighter through create, discover, fill, and finalize tools while using returned hole ids, option ids, and draft revisions.

The protocol acceptance scenario creates and finalizes a supported level-2 Fighter after the caller resolves the non-SRD synonym outside MCP and then follows returned progression, class choice, equipment, and loadout holes.

The protocol acceptance scenario creates and finalizes a supported level-2 Elf Soldier Wizard through returned cantrip, spellbook, prepared spell, equipment, loadout, and class-feature proficiency holes.

The protocol acceptance scenario verifies the finalized level-3 Wizard Character Sheet exposes four level-1 Spell Slots and two level-2 Spell Slots before battle, then verifies list_characters still exposes the durable sheet with one level-2 Spell Slot expended after battle handoff.

The protocol acceptance scenario reads list_characters after finalization and verifies the durable level-4 Wizard Character Sheet exposes Intelligence 17, 26 Hit Points, four level-1 Spell Slots, and three level-2 Spell Slots.

The protocol acceptance scenario reads list_characters after finalization and verifies the durable level-5 Wizard Character Sheet exposes Fireball Spell Access, 32 Hit Points, and unexpended level-1, level-2, and level-3 Spell Slots.

The protocol acceptance scenario finalizes the supported level-1 Orc Soldier Fighter, reads the resulting Character Sheet through list_characters, and verifies durable Hit Points before and after battle handoff.

The protocol acceptance scenario finalizes a supported level-2 Elf Soldier Wizard, verifies the Character Sheet exposes level-1 Spell Slots and selected spells, and later observes the expended slot after battle handoff.

The protocol acceptance scenario ends battle and inspects list_characters plus the session snapshot to prove durable Character Sheet Hit Points and Spell Slot expenditure remain visible to MCP callers.

The protocol acceptance scenario starts battle from the finalized level-3 Wizard and an SRD Sphinx of Wonder Stat Block, discovers the Scorching Ray act, fills returned target, attack-roll, and rolled-dice holes, and verifies one level-2 Spell Slot is expended.

The protocol acceptance scenario starts battle from the finalized level-4 Wizard and an SRD Sphinx of Wonder Stat Block, verifies the returned battle state carries four level-1 Spell Slots and three level-2 Spell Slots, and discovers the Scorching Ray battle act.

The protocol acceptance scenario starts battle from the finalized level-5 Wizard and an SRD Sphinx of Wonder Stat Block, discovers the Fireball battle act, fills returned saving throw and rolled-dice holes, and verifies one level-3 Spell Slot is expended.

The level-6 Rogue scenario reads the workflow guide result paths and catalog units before following returned Rogue 6 creation holes, durable Character Sheet state, and battle act subjects. Level-7 and level-8 add no new MCP tool workflow beyond these returned-state paths; their new runtime obligations stay in the support, QNT, and parity layers.

The level-6 Rogue scenario creates and finalizes an Orc Soldier Rogue 6 by selecting only returned progression, class, background, Ability Score Improvement, equipment, loadout, and Expertise option ids. The level-7 and level-8 scopes reuse this admitted default MCP creation vertical because character creation does not yet admit level-7 or level-8 progression options; no MCP evidence row is used as runtime support for those later-level mechanics.

The level-6 Rogue scenario reads list_characters after finalization and verifies the durable Rogue 6 Character Sheet exposes Hit Points, owned skill proficiencies, and the four selected Expertise proficiencies. Level-7 and level-8 support adds no new MCP sheet protocol shape; new supported mechanics remain covered by runtime and parity evidence.

The level-6 Rogue scenario starts battle from the finalized Rogue 6 Character Sheet, discovers the Steady Aim unit-feature act, resolves the no-hole subject, and verifies the returned battle state spends the Bonus Action and zeros movement for that combatant. Level-7 and level-8 reuse this MCP battle-flow evidence while Evasion and later-level runtime behavior remain validated by the support, QNT, and parity layers.
The protocol acceptance scenario selects SRD Stat Blocks for battle setup through select_stat_block after discovering valid Stat Block ids from list_stat_blocks.
The protocol acceptance scenario starts SRD battles from finalized Character Sheets and Stat Blocks, verifies the Initiative-derived turn order, and reads the current actor from the battle snapshot.

The protocol acceptance scenario discovers a returned Goblin Attack, fills its returned target, attack-roll, and interrupt holes, verifies the resolved result, rejects a pending-hole turn end without changing the current actor, and advances the returned turn.

The protocol acceptance scenario creates a finalized Fighter and Wizard roster, resolves a no-hole Action Surge through resolve_battle_act, then reuses the returned attack subject to supply target and attack-roll fills for a miss after the initial path includes rolled damage, and verifies the unchanged Hit Point projection.

The protocol acceptance scenario discovers action-time spell subjects for the level-2 Wizard, resolves Ray of Frost and Magic Missile through runtime-owned battle holes, and verifies Spell Slot expenditure.
The protocol acceptance scenario ends active battles through end_battle after combat resolution and verifies the battle handoff updates available Character Sheet state.

The protocol acceptance scenario verifies battle workflow recovery by rejecting end_turn and end_battle while battle holes are pending, requiring callers to continue with the current subject or rediscover state.

The level-9 Ranger scenario reads the MCP workflow guide and catalog units before selecting the returned Ranger 9 progression, class feature, spell access, equipment, loadout, character id, and battle result paths.

The level-9 Ranger scenario creates and finalizes an Orc Soldier Ranger 9 by following returned draft revisions, creation hole ids, and option ids, including Ranger level-9 Expertise and level-8 Ability Score Improvement selections.

The level-9 Ranger scenario lists the finalized Character Sheet and verifies durable Ranger 9 spell slots, prepared Spell Access, and the projected Expertise set that includes the level-9 Expertise choices.

The level-9 Ranger scenario starts battle from the returned Character Sheet id, verifies the returned battle id, turn order, unexpended spell-slot handoff, and discovers returned Ranger battle acts from the active battle state.

The level-10 Fighter Champion scenario reads the MCP workflow guide and catalog units before selecting the returned Fighter 10 progression, class feature, equipment, loadout, character id, and battle result paths.

The level-10 Fighter Champion scenario uses a focused MCP test fixture to admit Fighter 10, then creates and finalizes an Orc Soldier Fighter 10 by following returned draft revisions, creation hole ids, and option ids, including the five returned Fighter 10 Weapon Mastery options.

The level-10 Fighter Champion scenario lists the finalized Character Sheet and verifies durable Fighter 10 Hit Points, selected Champion subclass identity, selected Ability Score Improvement, and the five selected Weapon Mastery facts.

The level-10 Fighter Champion scenario starts battle from the returned Character Sheet id, verifies the returned battle id and turn order, discovers returned Fighter battle acts, and records the remaining blocker: Heroic Warrior is a passive turn-start runtime behavior with no returned MCP battle act or hole yet.

The real MCP protocol test routes finalized Character Session mutations through the shared operation surface, including supported class-level advancement and typed selection-replacement recovery, while preserving the canonical detail projection.

The real MCP row-coverage client calls query_character_session for both spellbookRitualAccesses and ritual spellInvocation, validates the returned ritual projections, and keeps query facts derived from the stored Character Sheet.
The real MCP row-coverage client calls retainOneAtATimeCompanion with the returned Character Session id and validates the retained companion projection before Battle admission.
The real MCP row-coverage client calls completeShortRest, completeLongRest, and an interrupted Long Rest with returned typed results through apply_character_session_operation.
The real MCP resource client calls both Font of Magic conversion directions and validates each typed Character Session result through apply_character_session_operation.
The real MCP initial-setup client calls start_battle in initialSetup mode, applies and rejects Initiative swaps, finalizes setup, and validates the returned setup and active Battle projections.
The real MCP row-coverage client calls replaceDruidWildShapeKnownForm on an admitted Druid Character Session and validates the canonical returned available detail.
The real MCP row-coverage client calls passCalendarTime for a resolved character and for a Stable character, copies the returned rolled-dice hole id, and validates the resolved fill outcome.
The real MCP row-coverage client successfully applies Prayer of Healing rest benefits to a returned recipient and validates the typed spell-rest result.
The real MCP Lay On Hands client calls applyLayOnHands and validates the returned healing result and follow-up operation envelope.

The real MCP resource client calls roll_dice for independent raw faces, then routes Uncanny Metabolism and Spell Access free-cast operations through the shared Character Session surface and validates their typed resource results.

The real MCP row-coverage client starts and ends a mixed Battle roster containing the returned Character Session, its retained companion admission, and an SRD Stat Block, validating companion and settlement projections.
The real MCP roster-lifecycle client calls battle_lifecycle addCombatant and removeCombatant for Stat Block and Character Session origins and validates occupancy and settlement recovery.

The real MCP row-coverage client discovers a returned Goblin Attack, fills its target and attack-roll holes, copies the presented Shield reaction choice, fills the interruptDecision hole, and validates the resolved result.

scopeAuditDecisions.reason: Task 5 added the executable create-level-three-wizard-and-cast-scorching-ray MCP acceptance scenario. Together with the reusable mcp-workflow-discovery scenario, level-1-3 now has scenario evidence for character creation, Character Sheet durability, and battle handoff using a level-3 SRD Wizard, Evoker subclass selection, level-2 Spell Slots, and Scorching Ray through returned battle holes.

Task 1 added the executable create-level-four-wizard-asi-and-battle-handoff MCP acceptance scenario. Together with the reusable workflow-discovery checks inside that scenario, level-1-4 now has scenario evidence for level-4 Wizard advancement, Ability Score Improvement selection, Character Sheet durability, and battle handoff.

Task 8 registered the executable create-level-five-wizard-fireball-and-battle-handoff MCP acceptance scenario. It covers workflow discovery, level-5 Wizard creation with Fireball through returned holes, durable Character Sheet state with level-3 Spell Slots, and battle handoff through returned Fireball battle holes.

Task 35 registered the executable create-level-six-rogue-expertise-and-steady-aim-battle-handoff MCP acceptance scenario. It covers workflow discovery, Rogue 6 character creation through returned holes, durable Character Sheet Expertise projection, and Steady Aim battle handoff through returned battle act subjects.

Level-1-7 adds supported Evasion runtime obligations plus closed class/spell accounting, but no new MCP tool workflow shape beyond workflow discovery, character creation, Character Sheet read, and battle handoff. The existing level-6 Rogue vertical is the admitted default MCP character-creation path for this scope and already follows returned draft revisions, option ids, character ids, battle ids, and battle subjects; Evasion support remains proven by the support, QNT/generator, and MBT/parity layers rather than by MCP evidence.

Level-1-8 adds repeated ASI, numeric progression, and Wild Shape threshold accounting that is closed outside MCP workflow execution; it does not introduce a new MCP tool flow beyond the four existing required flows. The existing level-6 Rogue vertical remains the admitted default MCP character-creation path for this scope and proves returned-state sequencing for creation, sheet, and battle handoff, while level-8 mechanics stay covered by support completeness and parity layers.
